explanation: Coleridge said the poem came to him in a dream, and the rest slipped away during the visit. Writers still call an unwelcome interrupter 'a person from Porlock'.

claims.text: In the preface to Kubla Khan, published in 1816, Coleridge says he was interrupted by 'a person on business from Porlock' while writing the poem down.
Christabel, Frost at Midnight and Dejection: An Ode are other Coleridge poems with no link to the visitor from Porlock.
Coleridge said the lines of Kubla Khan came to him during a dream-like sleep and that he lost the rest after the interruption.
The phrase 'a person from Porlock' is used for an unwelcome interrupter of creative work.
